quiz.title: Integration by Partial Fractions Quiz (Ex 7.5)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the partial-fraction method from Exercise 7.5 — proper vs improper fractions, distinct and repeated linear factors, and irreducible quadratics. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Integration by partial fractions, NCERT Class 12 Exercise 7.5

questions.q: Before splitting a rational function into partial fractions, it must be a proper fraction. Which of these is already proper?
questions.explanation: A fraction is proper when the numerator degree is less than the denominator degree. x/(x² − 1) has degree 1 over degree 2, so it is proper. The others have numerator degree ≥ denominator degree.

questions.q: For the improper fraction (x² + 1)/(x + 1), what must you do first?
options: Divide to get a polynomial plus a proper remainder fraction
questions.explanation: When the fraction is improper, do polynomial long division first. (x² + 1)/(x + 1) = (x − 1) + 2/(x + 1); only the proper part 2/(x + 1) needs further work.

questions.q: The correct partial-fraction form of 1/[(x − 1)(x − 2)] is:
questions.explanation: Two distinct linear factors each get a single constant numerator: A/(x − 1) + B/(x − 2).

questions.q: Solving 1/[(x − 1)(x − 2)] = A/(x − 1) + B/(x − 2), the values are:
questions.explanation: Multiply out: 1 = A(x − 2) + B(x − 1). Put x = 1: 1 = A(−1), so A = −1. Put x = 2: 1 = B(1), so B = 1.

questions.q: For a repeated linear factor, the fraction 1/[(x − 1)²(x + 2)] must be written as:
questions.explanation: A repeated factor (x − 1)² contributes two terms, A/(x − 1) and B/(x − 1)², and the distinct factor (x + 2) contributes C/(x + 2).

questions.q: For an irreducible quadratic factor, the correct numerator in the partial fraction is:
questions.explanation: An irreducible quadratic such as (x² + 1) takes a linear numerator (Ax + B)/(x² + 1), because the numerator degree is one less than the denominator degree.
Using A = −1, B = 1, the integral is −log|x − 1| + log|x − 2| + C = log|(x − 2)/(x − 1)| + C.

questions.q: Which substitution turns 1/[x(x² + 1)] type problems into an easier partial-fraction split when only even powers of x appear?
questions.explanation: When the expression depends on x² (for example 1/[x(x² + 1)] handled via x dx), the substitution t = x² converts it to a rational function in t that splits with simple partial fractions.

faq.q: What is Exercise 7.5 in NCERT Class 12 Maths about?
faq.a: Exercise 7.5 covers integration by partial fractions. You learn to break a rational function into simpler fractions — using distinct linear factors, repeated factors and irreducible quadratic factors — and then integrate each piece.

faq.q: When can I apply the partial-fraction method?
faq.a: Only to a proper rational function, where the numerator degree is less than the denominator degree. If the fraction is improper, first divide to get a polynomial plus a proper remainder, then split the remainder into partial fractions.

faq.q: How do I handle a repeated linear factor like (x − 1)²?
faq.a: A repeated factor needs one term for each power. For (x − 1)² write A/(x − 1) + B/(x − 1)². Missing the second term is the most common mistake students make in this exercise.

faq.q: What numerator goes over an irreducible quadratic factor?
faq.a: Use a linear numerator of the form (Ax + B) over a factor like (x² + 1). After splitting, such terms usually integrate to a log and an arctan expression.
